title: NRI Seafarers Can Now Use a Job Contract or Seaman's Book to Open an NPS Account
excerpt: PFRDA's November 13 circular lets NRI seafarers use a valid employment contract or a Continuous Discharge Certificate with a disembarkation record under six months old as proof of address for NPS Tier I accounts.
body:
• PFRDA Circular No. PFRDA/2026/55/REG-POP/10, dated November 13, 2026, lets NRI seafarers open an NPS Tier I account using an employment contract or a recent Continuous Discharge Certificate as proof of address.
  • A CDC works only if its disembarkation stamp or record is not more than six months old; the employment contract route is for a seafarer proceeding on a fresh contract.
  • Seafarers currently onboard a ship may give either their employer's overseas address or their own Indian address as their current address.
  • The relaxation covers proof of address only — identity verification and all other KYC, due-diligence and anti-money-laundering requirements are unchanged, and it took effect on November 13, 2026.

NRI seafarers opening a National Pension System (NPS) Tier I account no longer have to produce conventional overseas address proof — a document many cannot furnish because their workplace is a ship. In a circular dated November 13, 2026, the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) directed every regulated entity to accept either a valid employment contract or a Continuous Discharge Certificate (CDC) as proof of address for an NRI subscriber with a seafarer work profile. The full text of the circular is reproduced by TaxGuru, and Outlook Money has summarised what subscribers need to know.

Who is affected — exactly

The change applies to NRI subscribers with a seafarer work profile who are opening an NPS Tier I account. It does not change the rules for other NRI or OCI subscribers, and it does not waive identity proof or any other part of onboarding. PFRDA said seafarers were finding it difficult to provide overseas address proof at the time of onboarding, and prescribed these documents specifically to verify both employment and non-resident status.

What changed, precisely

Before the amendment, NRI and OCI onboarding followed the KYC framework in PFRDA's circular of December 2, 2025, built on the KYC/AML/CFT Master Circular of September 25, 2025 — including standard proof-of-identity and proof-of-address documents, with customer due diligence and, where applicable, enhanced due diligence. The November 13 circular inserts a new point (iv) into the note to paragraph 8.3(a) of that framework. For a seafarer, regulated entities must now accept any one of two documents as proof of address: a valid employment contract with the employer or shipping company, where the seafarer is proceeding on a fresh contract; or a Continuous Discharge Certificate whose disembarkation stamp or record is not more than six months old.

There is a second, practical concession for seafarers who apply while they are at sea. A subscriber currently onboard a ship may furnish either the overseas address of the employer or the subscriber's own Indian address as the current address.

When it applies

The circular, issued under Section 14(1) of the PFRDA Act, 2013, took effect from the date of its issuance — November 13, 2026. It is addressed to all Points of Presence, Central Recordkeeping Agencies, the NPS Trust and other stakeholders, and every other provision of the December 2025 circular and the September 2025 Master Circular remains unchanged.

What to do next

If you are an NRI seafarer opening an NPS Tier I account, take one of the two accepted documents to your Point of Presence or CRA: your current employment contract if you are about to join a ship on a fresh contract, or your CDC — checking first that the latest disembarkation stamp is within six months. If you are applying from onboard, be ready to give either your employer's overseas address or your Indian address as your current address. Expect the rest of onboarding — identity documents and due-diligence checks — to proceed exactly as before, because the relaxation is confined to proof of address.
